mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the observed mean return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the cumulative return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode corporate profit margins and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the observed mean return is not statistically below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the federal funds rate and mortgage interest rates (proxied by RSAFS) above their respective 12-month averages signals a tightening in both monetary and credit conditions, which increases borrowing costs and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month MA and RSAFS > 12-month MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based expansion in demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA and HOUST > 12-month MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports wage growth and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically above zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period where the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds the federal funds rate by more than 200 basis points for six consecutive months indicates real interest rates are negative, which incentivizes risk-taking and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not statistically above zero at 90% confidence.
